newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA UNDECIDED ON BONDS TO WIPE OUT OIL DEFICIT.
newsitem.headline: INDIA UNDECIDED ON BONDS TO WIPE OUT OIL DEFICIT.

text.p: The Indian government is yet to decide on the terms of a 10-year bond issue to pay off the 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) it owes to state-run oil companies, a Petroleum Ministry official said on Tuesday.
"The general agreement is to issue promisssory notes but the lock-in period and the rate of interest payable on the bonds could not be resolved," said the official, who asked not to be identified.
The official said that the finance Ministry was opposed to the Petroleum Ministry's suggestion to pay an interest rate of 10.5 percent on the bonds.
"The nature of the bonds have been agreed. It will be in the form of promissory notes worded to allow oil companies to pledge them further," he said.

The 155-billion rupee debt was accumulated during 1996-97 (April-March) because oil firms had to sell crude and petroleum products below the cost of production to support India's complex cross-subsidy system known as the administered pricing mechanism.
The government's delay in repaying them has presented state-run oil companies with a severe liquidity crunch.
Oil firms have been urging the government to pay back the money they are owed, saying further delays could seriously hamper their ability to pay for refinery feedstock and long-term investment.
Officials are struggling to find an option that would limit the size of any needed fuel price rises. ($1 = 35.7 rupees)
